negative_findings.description: No Temenos or Sopra Banking Software press release naming a Hungarian bank go-live was found; results returned only generic global core-banking marketing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor newsrooms searched in English returned no HU-specific core banking implementation announcement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: HU core-banking supplier landscape appears dominated by domestic/regional integrators (Takarékinfo, T-Systems, Capsys, Laurel) rather than the big international core vendors — or those wins are simply unannounced. Either way the international-vendor newsroom route is low-yield for HU core banking.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The commissioning organisation's own regional presence is not discoverable through generic HU search, implying HU-market vendor visibility generally requires direct site crawls rather than search-engine discovery — a systematic bias to correct for.

coverage_gaps.description: POS terminal hardware vendors (Ingenico/Worldline, Verifone, PAX, Castles) and their HU distributors/bank customers were not covered in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated hu+en pass on 'POS terminál forgalmazó', 'terminálpark', 'kártyaelfogadó terminál szállító' plus each hardware brand + Magyarország.

coverage_gaps.description: Central infrastructure operators that sit between banks and vendors (GIRO Zrt., BISZ Zrt., Bankkártya/scheme processors) were not profiled, though their supplier announcements name participating private banks.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile giro.hu and bisz.hu news/tender pages and their vendor announcements as a bridge between the public and private supplier ecosystems.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor case-study libraries were reached via search engines only; no direct in-site case-study search (site: queries, sitemap crawl) was performed for the major vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each vendor in the actor map, crawl its sitemap/case-study index directly and grep for HU bank names and 'Hungary'/'Magyarország' — search engines under-index marketing PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: Few vendor sources found so far disclose HU-specific unit counts; the Diebold/UniCredit ~180 ATM figure and the MNB-mandated 1,039-unit allocation are the main quantified anchors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prioritise sources with numeric disclosure discipline: listed-issuer reports (ANY Nyrt., 4iG Nyrt., Euronet Worldwide IR) and regulator documents, over marketing case studies.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language searching worked well for cash logistics, ATM mandates and domestic integrators, but produced almost nothing for card-personalisation contract news and nothing for international vendor case studies (which exist in English only).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept an asymmetric strategy: hu for domestic suppliers/regulatory demand signals, en for international vendor announcements; add hu terms 'megszemélyesítés', 'kártyagyártó', 'szállítói szerződés' to the personalisation pass.

brief: Hungary's private-bank supplier ecosystem is legible mainly from the vendor side: international vendors (ACI Worldwide, Tietoevry, Diebold Nixdorf) publish named HU bank deployments with occasional unit counts, while the domestic layer (Capsys, T-Systems Magyarorszag, Laurel, Takarekinfo, 4iG, CARDNET) exposes bank relationships through Hungarian-language reference and news pages that search engines index poorly. The highest-value quantified anchors are not vendor marketing at all but regulator-forced disclosure — the GVH 2019 card-acceptance sectoral inquiry and MNB decree 19/2025, which allocates 1,039 mandated ATMs bank-by-bank (OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104) and thereby telegraphs the 2025-2026 ATM procurement pipeline. Cash-cycle suppliers are visible as CIT operators (G4S, MPT Security, Criterion) but the banknote-equipment vendor layer and the POS hardware vendor layer remain unmapped. Recommended next step is direct sitemap-level crawling of vendor case-study libraries plus profiling of GIRO/BISZ, since search-engine discovery systematically under-represents this cell.
